review.description: Notification S1-S4 retain verified callbacks, stable signed delivery identities, retry behavior and expiration; GitHub response-cache retention does not modify host subscription delivery.
review.implementation: No internal/events callback, subscription or delivery code changed. The generic store addition only inventories metadata in a supplied bucket and the provider caller supplies github-cache. Eviction inventories only CheckedAt and Expires alongside authoritative storage IDs and decoded body sizes. Unselected bodies, Header, ETag and Redirect payloads remain in SQLite. Field names, byte path and kind are bound values; cursor closure permits subsequent mutation within the same transaction. The durable response itself remains unchanged, and in-memory changes follow durable commit.
review.tests: Read TestSubscriptionVerificationRetryDedupRefreshAndExpiry: a repeated subscribe preserves identity, a503 retries the same event ID, acknowledged delivery is not repeated, expired subscriptions do not deliver and unsubscribe is idempotent. Cache tests assert unrelated stored response peers survive eviction. TestJSONByteEntriesKeepBodylessMetadataAndTransactionalIdentity seeds five rows with 128 KiB each of Link, ETag and Redirect data; selected CheckedAt/ID metadata stays within 128 bytes and two fields per row. It checks authoritative IDs/decoded sizes, bound bucket/path/field inputs, empty selection and unchanged persisted body/ETag after mutation. TestGitHubPersistentCacheEvictionKeepsLargeHeadersAfterRestart seeds two 1 MiB Link responses, retires the 25 hour old row and preserves the fresh exact Link/body through restart. Both use temporary SQLite state; the provider fixture has a 10 second failure bound and deferred cleanup.
